events.text: Today we are reading decimals through thousandths.

events.text: We will name each place, work out the value of a digit, and investigate why some zeros matter while others leave the amount unchanged.

events.text: Our learning goal is to read and explain decimal place value to thousandths.

events.text: To the right of the decimal point come tenths, hundredths and thousandths.
events.spoken_punctuation: To the right of the decimal point come tenths, hundredths and thousandths.

events.text: Each place is one tenth of the place to its left.

events.text: A digit gives the number of those units; its position gives their size.

events.text: Read four point three zero seven.
events.spoken_punctuation: Read four point three zero seven.

events.text: The four represents four ones, the three represents three tenths, and the seven represents seven thousandths.
events.spoken_punctuation: The four represents four ones, the three represents three tenths, and the seven represents seven thousandths.

events.text: There are no hundredths.

events.text: The zero keeps the seven in the thousandths place.
events.spoken_punctuation: The zero keeps the seven in the thousandths place.

events.text: Without that zero, four point three seven would have seven hundredths, a different amount.
events.spoken_punctuation: Without that zero, four point three seven would have seven hundredths, a different amount!

events.text: Find the value of the six in twelve point zero six four.

events.text: The six is the second digit after the decimal point.

events.text: The six represents six hundredths, or zero point zero six.

events.text: What is the value of the eight in five point two one eight?
